## Constitution Check
## Design decisions
## Found and left
## Knobs this plan takes (the record could not settle them)
## Project Structure
## Risks
## Summary
## Technical Context
## The 451 parts this feature takes over
## The phases - each usable on its own
## What retires (451 T302 part 4) and when
### D1 - the lane's tree: the existing landing worktree, adopted into the pool as the lane's reserved tree
### D10 - FR-001's gate-write guard and 451 T405's tree check, by construction plus a fixture
### D11 - what retires, and when (451 T302 parts 1 and 4)
### D12 - the measurement (FR-006, FR-007, FR-010)
### D13 - the coordinator's own commits go out before a builder builds on them
### D14 - done refs, successors and repairs
### D15 - where the code lives
### D2 - what drives the lane: a detached runner of our own, `l7r-gate lane --work`
### D3 - the hand-in's "rebase": the builder's diff applied onto `origin/main` with the carry's rules, then the first pass, then the commit
### D4 - the first pass at hand-in: what a builder can answer is asked; what is the lane's is not
### D5 - when the lane starts a batch, and what it holds (FR-004, 451 T415)
### D6 - a red batch: attribute, else halve; eject; land the rest (US4)
### D7 - the repair: a queue entry a fresh builder takes (US4, US5)
### D8 - the lane's states and its log
### D9 - the coordinator's wake-up: one background command, one status line a batch (FR-005)
preamble

decisions.summary: An ejected change or a carry conflict becomes a repair entry in the queue that a fresh builder takes, not an agent the lane launches.
decisions.why: The GM-approved sketch item 1 says it outright: 'the ejected task returns to the queue as a repair entry'. Item 3 has the coordinator as the dispatcher ('I'd dispatch'), and a builder the coordinator dispatches for the entry is a fresh agent that is neither standing nor the coordinator. The coordinator's context gets one queue line. Nothing asked for is narrowed.

decisions.id: XVI-a / D9 + Risks (judgment wakes with no fresh agent)
decisions.summary: Besides repair entries, the lane wakes the coordinator for a set red twice / arbiter owed (D6 step 4), the push failing twice after a re-run (Risks), and the runner dying (D9). The plan does not say who does the integration work after the wake.
decisions.why: Sketch item 3: 'The only integration work left to me would be the rare case that needs judgment, and there a fresh agent per batch beats me doing it'; the plan's own quote of US5 is 'never a standing integrator, never the coordinator's context'. D7 is presented as the plan's answer to US5, but it covers only ejected changes and carry conflicts. A batch that is green but cannot push twice, and a set the arbiter is asked about, wake the coordinator, and the plan names no fresh agent for that batch, which by default leaves the work in the coordinator's turns. That is exactly the case the GM gave to a fresh agent. No impossibility is claimed and none exists, since D7's repair entry could carry them. (A dead runner needs only `make lane-start`, which is a dispatch, not integration, and is fine.)

decisions.summary: Inside the lane, the red-gate tripwire does not fire on consecutive reds that are steps of one halving.
decisions.why: Applied literally, the tripwire would stop the lane at the second step of any bisection. That defeats the GM-approved sketch item 1 ('On a red result it bisects and ejects the failing change') and FR-004, and the plan says so concretely. Exempting a halving's own steps is legitimate.

decisions.id: XVI-b / D6 step 4, part 2 (everything else the set key exempts)
decisions.summary: The exemption is implemented by keying the tripwire to 'a second red of the SAME sorted set of short shas'. That exempts every lane red, not only a halving's steps.
decisions.why: Judged by its purpose, the key leaves the tripwire unable to fire. Every path the plan names gives a fresh set. Halving runs strictly smaller subsets. After an attributed ejection 'the rest runs again' as a new set. The last survivor is 'ejected without a run of its own'. A repair's hand-in supersedes with a NEW sha (D7, D14), so a task that goes red, is repaired, and goes red again never matches. The Risks re-run follows a GREEN gate, so it can give at most one red. Phase 2 states the result itself: the tripwire by change set 'never sees one set twice'. Phase 3's Verify line ('fires on a second red of one set') tests a state the lane never produces. The tripwire is one of the existing `make land` checks (D4 lists it among the first pass's checks) that FR-003 says the lane runs and FR-008 says is not dropped. This exception is plausible at the level of wording but empties the check. Required: inside the lane it must still be able to fire on repeated red on the same work, for example a repair's hand-in red again, or one task ejected twice, while staying quiet on a halving's own steps. The plan says how and tests a path that the lane can actually reach.

decisions.id: XVI-c / D3 (rebase as a no-commit apply)
decisions.summary: FR-002's 'rebases onto current main' is done as the builder's diff applied onto origin/main with carry.rs's merge rules (cherry-pick -n) and then committed, because the project forbids git rebase.
decisions.why: The request's purpose ('Conflicts and bookkeeping refusals then get fixed by the builder that has the context, in its own tree') is met in full. The work ends on current main, conflicts stop in the builder's tree for the builder to resolve, and then the first pass and the commit follow in FR-002's order. The only thing lost is the builder's intermediate commits, which nothing asks for. This is a mechanism, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: In phase 1 the hand-in applies onto the clone's HEAD rather than origin/main; from phase 2 onto origin/main.
decisions.why: In phase 1 the coordinator still lands from its clone, so the clone's HEAD is the main that the work lands on. Applying onto origin/main would put the work on a base without the staged work it was handed out on, which defeats the stated purpose of a hand-in that 'arrives on what it lands on'. From phase 2 the literal origin/main holds. This is a purpose-level justification and is temporary.

decisions.summary: The hand-in asks the first-pass checks a builder can answer and leaves writer_refusal, the mark's hold, the tripwire, claims-in-flight and the gate stamp rows to the lane, which asks them again when it lands.
decisions.why: FR-002 says 'the landing's cheap first pass'. The left-out checks either cannot be answered before a gate (the stamp rows are physically impossible), concern another writer or the ordering of other tasks, or refuse for reasons no builder can cure. Asking them in a builder's tree would defeat the sketch's purpose of having builders fix what they have the context to fix. All of them are still asked at landing, so FR-008 holds. No coverage runs, as FR-002 requires.

decisions.summary: LANE_MAX=6 and LANE_WAIT_S=0 are seeded from the two-tier ceiling and the trial's 'stronger version', because trial 458 has no finding yet; its verdict resets both.
decisions.why: FR-004 seeds the knob from trial 458's finding, and that finding does not exist yet, so seeding from it is impossible today. The GM told the session to start now. The plan labels both values GUESS and commits to resetting them from the trial's verdict.

decisions.id: D5 batch membership vs FR-003 'in order'
decisions.summary: A batch takes every waiting hand-in of the OLDEST hand-in's feature, so a later hand-in of that feature goes ahead of an earlier hand-in of another feature.
decisions.why: FR-003 says the lane 'takes hand-ins from the done refs in order', and D5 itself reads that as hand-in order ('oldest first'). The reason given, that `make land` takes one F=, does not require a reorder. A batch made of the oldest hand-in plus the CONSECUTIVE same-feature hand-ins after it keeps one F= and keeps the order. The reorder buys larger batches, which is a design preference and not one of the grounds for an exception. Required: keep hand-in order, or state the departure as an exception to FR-003 that is ruled on.

decisions.summary: Until phase 3, a red that the gate's record cannot place ejects the whole batch as one repair entry instead of halving.
decisions.why: This is rollout order, not a narrowing of the finished feature: phase 3 in this same plan replaces it with the halving and 'land the rest'. Under XV a phase-3 stall would leave it standing, so FR-004 is met only once phase 3 lands, and the feature is not done until then. Its one entry covers the whole batch, so it is also a fresh agent per batch.

decisions.id: D12 LIKE-window test omits machine load
decisions.summary: A window is LIKE when it holds 8 or more hours of builder work and its time-weighted trees held is within 0.5 of the night's; the machine's load is read but is not part of the test.
decisions.why: FR-010 defines a LIKE window as one whose 'concurrency is close ...: trees held, time-weighted ..., and the machine's load'. The load is one of the two named components, and it is the GM's seventh-message concern ('how much was happening at the time') on a shared container. D12 drops it from the likeness test without saying so, and phase 5 picks 'the first like window' by that test. A window of three trees under very different load would count as like. No justification is given, and the load median is already available (`make sampler-report`). Required: the likeness test includes a load band (a GUESS), and where load differs, both loads are stated beside the figure. Phase 5 already states each figure with its concurrency, so this finding is confined to the likeness test.

decisions.summary: The lane runs in the existing <clone>-land worktree, adopted into the pool under a reserved holder outside the cap.
decisions.why: The spec leaves the tree to the plan. FR-003's 'its own worktree' is met.

decisions.summary: The lane is a detached `l7r-gate lane --work` runner under flock, using the project's runner pattern; the Workflow tool and the Refinery were priced and not taken whole.
decisions.why: The sketch says 'run as a script in its own worktree rather than in my turns'. FR-009's reuse question is answered and recorded (R1).

decisions.summary: Each attempt gets its own file; attribution comes from the gate's Phase lines; halving lands as it goes and ejects the last survivor without a run of its own; there is no flake retry.
decisions.why: This is FR-004 and the sketch's 'bisects and ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands'. Nothing pushes ungated (FR-008).

decisions.summary: Repair entries live in the common git dir; the queue serves repairs first (LANE_REPAIR_FIRST).
decisions.why: The entries stay out of the coordinator's tree (FR-001), and the knob is labeled.

decisions.summary: States are computed from refs and an append-only lane log; 'carried' is read against origin/main.
decisions.why: This is internal mechanism and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The wake-up is `make lane-wait` in the background, one status line per batch; a Stop-guard rule refuses the main session's stop while lane work waits and no lane-wait runs; the prompt hook prints unread lines.
decisions.why: FR-005's wake-up. The Stop rule's reach is only what makes FR-005's wake happen, which is enforcement of the request.

decisions.id: D10 guard fixture, T405 option C
decisions.summary: FR-001 holds because gates run only in the lane tree, pinned by a fixture over two trees; T405 closes by its option (C).
decisions.why: This enforces FR-001.

decisions.summary: After a like window of lane landings, `make land` outside the lane tree is refused (LAND_HERE_OK escape) and land-alone steps 1-6 retire; step 7 moves to take-tip.sh; writers.rs stays.
decisions.why: The refusal enforces FR-001 and makes the lane the one route. Keeping writers.rs honors FR-008.

decisions.summary: One measurement script over both windows: tokens by actor as window totals, task size beside each figure, concurrency stated with each figure, the before figure taken in phase 0.
decisions.why: This is FR-006, FR-007 and FR-010 apart from the likeness test ruled above. Fresh integration agents are left out of the actor list because D7 makes them repair builders, and FR-006 still counts them.

decisions.id: D13 handout refused on unpushed clone commits
decisions.summary: A handout is refused while the clone holds commits that origin/main lacks; the coordinator pushes spec-only filings DIRECT.
decisions.why: This is required by D3's base, and it honors US1's 'nothing it writes waits on a gate' with the existing DIRECT route. The moved coverage premise is measured, not built around.

decisions.summary: A successor or repair handout applies the earlier done commit uncommitted and supersedes its ref; it waits only on an open batch.
decisions.why: Internal mechanism that serves the sketch.

decisions.summary: One new crate; phases 0-5; the knob table.
decisions.why: No decision here narrows the request.

decisions.summary: The lane's tree is the existing <clone>-land worktree, adopted into the pool under a reserved holder outside the cap; knob L7R_LANE_TREE.
decisions.why: FR-003 asks for a worktree of its own and the spec leaves which one to the plan; choosing an existing tree with a warm cache is a design choice inside that.

decisions.summary: 451 T525 (remove the -land worktree when land-alone retires, so the sweep takes its cache) is replaced, not taken over: the worktree stays as the lane's tree and phase 4 closes T525 in 451 with a pointer.
decisions.why: Ruled on D1's own account of T525, since T525's line is not in the bundle and the repository was not read. On that account T525's premise is a DEAD tree once land-alone retires; under this feature the tree is live (the lane gates in it), so the trigger T525 waits on never arises and nothing of 461's request or spec is narrowed. Leaving T525 open would have a later task delete the lane's tree, which would defeat FR-003; closing it with a pointer is the consistent act. The disk question T525 served is not dropped: D11 measures whether the clone's own 104 GB target directory can go once no gate builds there.

The lane never lands and the coordinator is never told, which defeats FR-003 and FR-005 together. It meets none of the three tests. It is not impossible: the block prices the fix at about four lines and one test, where wake::dead counts any owed line naming the open batch since the last start as having told the death, and T14's red line already says the runner stopped and the batch is open. It is not implied by the GM's words. And the literal rule does not defeat the purpose. The reason given for leaving it, 'dead weight once T15 lands', is a code-economy argument, and that does not make an exception legitimate. T23 landing after T14-T22 does not establish that T22's base flip sends no real hand-in to the lane before T15. ### T15 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Phase 2: a red unit naming no change or several, or no unit read, ejects the whole batch as one `unplaced` entry
decisions.why: Interim stage of FR-004's 'attribute, else bisect': the block states T24 replaces attribute() with D6's halving over candidates, so the request's 'bisects and ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands' is delivered by phase 3. Within ONLY on that premise; if phase 3 does not replace this path, whole-batch ejection of innocent changes would be a narrowing of the request.

decisions.summary: A crate is its directory; dependents not counted; a dependent's red is unplaced until phase 3 halving
decisions.why: Conservative: a dependent's red yields unplaced (no innocent change named) and the phase 3 halving places it; nothing of the request narrowed.

decisions.summary: A Phase line naming several crates is one unit over all of them (a family cover-build red no longer ejects an innocent change)
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome (an innocent change ejected as red) toward the request's 'ejects the failing change'. Open question for the author, not ruled: the line prints the first 3 crates and '(+<k> more)'; the block does not say how a line with k>0 is read. If read as naming only the 3, a change touching a named crate is still ejected for a culprit in a hidden one - the same defect this decision fixes. State it (e.g. k>0 reads as unplaced, or the lane's NAMED is set to name all).

decisions.summary: A hook suite maps to a delta path by the guard file name and the guard and shared-guard sources
decisions.why: Attribution mapping detail serving FR-004's attribute step; a missed map falls to unplaced, never to an innocent ejection.

decisions.summary: A first-pass row maps by a delta path in its text or its leading task list
decisions.why: Attribution mapping detail serving FR-004; a row with no match is not attributed to a change.

decisions.summary: Any non-zero exit (not -1) is red, so a first-pass refusal naming no change - a hold, a lock, an owed claims round - ejects the whole batch `unplaced` and files a repair entry for every task, where T14 stopped the runner
decisions.why: The request: 'On a red result it bisects and ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands, and the ejected task returns to the queue as a repair entry.' Here no change fails and the block says so ('though none is at fault'), yet every change is ejected and sent to a fresh builder, and none lands. Grounds: not physically impossible (T14 stopped the runner in this case, so a non-ejecting path exists); not implied by the GM's words; the literal rule does not defeat the purpose - this decision does, since repair builders with nothing to repair are pure token cost (FR-006 counts repair builders) and a persisting hold or lock refuses the resubmissions again. Its stated reason, 'the algorithmically easier route', is the not-legitimate kind. It also contradicts the block's own Decision 3, which calls ejecting an innocent change a defect. Taken case by case: a lock and a hold are environmental and name no change, so ejecting is NOT LEGITIMATE for each; an owed claims round that belongs to a batch task is attributable, so map it to that task (Decision 5's task-list route) rather than eject the batch, and if it cannot be mapped it is not a change's failure either. Unlike D1, this rule sits in the runner's red classification, and nothing in the block says T24 replaces it. What it should say instead: a refusal naming no change ejects nothing; the runner stops with the batch open (as T14, or as exit -1 below) or waits and retries, and wakes the coordinator only as FR-005 and US5 allow.

decisions.summary: Exit -1 (make could not start or was killed) ejects nothing; the runner stops with the batch open, its owed line carrying stopped: true
decisions.why: Ejects no innocent change and lands nothing unchecked (FR-008); a stop on an infrastructure failure is not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Only a non-zero exit 'not on origin/main' counts as red (a red already present on main is not blamed on the batch)
decisions.why: Read as: a red reproduced on origin/main is not the batch's change's fault, so nothing is ejected for it; that serves 'ejects the failing change'.

decisions.summary: A kill between filing an entry and its eject lines resumes as a new attempt; an entry is a change's repair only where an eject line names it
decisions.why: Crash-recovery detail; the consumer rule (T16 reads repairs by eject lines) keeps any change the resume lands from being repaired, so no request clause is narrowed. Its cost is an entry's `ejected` field that can overstate, and the block states that cost.

decisions.summary: Only the runner's own stopped: true line tells a death (T20's rule revisited)
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome (a runner killed after an ejection never said to the coordinator), serving FR-005's wake. 'Narrowed' here describes the death signal, not the request.

decisions.summary: The attribution reads Phase lines where the gate's writer files them (pool holder, then feature_of via SPECIFY_FEATURE); the real lane-tree observation deferred to T23
decisions.why: Implementation reading pinned by a test with the real writer; deferring the real-tree observation to the lane's first real batch narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Suite and row readers read the attempt file; the --src hooks Phase-line fallback is not built
decisions.why: Implementation reading of where the output lands; an unbuilt fallback the request never named narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Each ejection writes one `owed` line for each entry and the runner goes on (unlabeled; Approach)
decisions.why: Bookkeeping for repair entries (FR-004). Whether an owed line wakes the coordinator against FR-005's 'once per landed batch, otherwise only for US5's cases' cannot be settled from this bundle (US5 not supplied); D8 makes only the stopped line a death, so it is taken as not an extra wake.

blocks: ### T15 (phase 2's red path: a red batch attributed from the gate's own record, its changes ejected as repair entries, the rest run again)
### T15 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: In phase 2, a red unit that names no change or more than one, or no unit read at all, is UNPLACED and ejects the batch as one repair entry (why unplaced); phase 3's halving (T24) replaces attribute().
decisions.why: The request's sketch says 'it bisects and ejects the failing change', and FR-004 says 'attribute, else bisect'. T15 is the attribute half. The block says phase 3's halving (T24) replaces attribute(), inside this feature. Until then the else-branch hands the batch to a fresh builder as a queue entry, not to the coordinator, so SC-003's 'no batch is repaired whole by the coordinator' holds. This is the order of delivery, not a carve-out from the end state. It becomes a narrowing if T24 is dropped or deferred out of the feature.

decisions.summary: A crate is its directory; dependents are not counted, so a core change that reddens lane's tests is unplaced and left to phase 3's halving.
decisions.why: The block labels this D6's literal 'a crate by its directory'; D6's text is not in the bundle. On the request and FR-004 alone, it is within: attribution is a best-effort first step with bisect behind it, and this rule never ejects an innocent change, it only falls through to the fallback.

decisions.summary: A Phase line naming several crates is one unit over all of them (a family cover-build is one compile); only the printed form is cut, using a GUESS display knob.
decisions.why: It fixes a wrong outcome: reading one crate at a time ejected an innocent change as red, which goes against 'ejects the failing change'. It is pinned by a named test. The NAMED knob only shortens a printed line and decides no behavior.

decisions.summary: A hook suite maps to a delta path matching tests/hooks/test-<stem>.*, and for a *-hooks stem also the guard sources in rust/guard/src/guards and rust/guard/shared/src/guards.
decisions.why: The block labels this D6's map; D6 is not in the bundle. Within on the request: including the shared crate only widens what a suite reaches, and an ambiguous result is unplaced and goes to the fallback. Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: A first-pass refusal row maps to a change by a delta path its text contains, or by its leading task list.
decisions.why: The block labels this D6's 'a row by its file', plus the first pass's own row form. It is mechanism inside the attribution FR-004 asks for. What happens to a row that maps to SEVERAL changes is ruled under 6c.

decisions.summary: Exit -1 (make could not start, or was killed) ejects nothing: the runner stops with the batch open and an owed line carrying stopped:true, and the next lane-start resumes.
decisions.why: This is an exception to 'a non-zero exit is a red that ejects', judged separately from 6b to 6d. The GM's rule is 'on a red result it bisects and ejects the failing change'. An exit -1 is no result of any change: the checks did not run, or ran to no verdict. There is no failing change to name, so the literal rule cannot be applied, and ejecting on no evidence would eject innocent changes, defeating the rule's purpose of letting the rest land. Stopping keeps the batch. The wake this adds is not a per-landed-batch wake. FR-005 allows other wakes only for US5's cases, and US5's text is not in the bundle. On the request, though, it is the 'rare case that needs judgment' that the sketch's item 3 leaves to the coordinator.

decisions.summary: A first-pass refusal whose every row names NO change of the batch (a hold, a lock, an owed round of no task of the batch) ejects nothing and stops the runner with the batch open; the next lane-start resumes it.
decisions.why: Scoped to the stated class only: every row names no change of the batch. The request's object is 'the failing change', and a refusal caused by something outside the batch has none, so the literal rule cannot be applied. The request's purpose, that the rest of the batch lands, cannot be reached either: the same refusal blocks the rest and would refuse every repair of any ejected change. This also reverses the whole-batch ejection that round 1 ruled NOT LEGITIMATE. On the wake it adds, see 6a: US5 is not in the bundle, and the request's ground is the sketch's item 3.

decisions.id: T15 Decision 6c (unlabeled; found in Decision 6's trigger)
decisions.summary: A first-pass refusal with a row that names MORE THAN ONE change of the batch, for example Decision 5's leading task list 'T13, T14: ...' with the two tasks in different hand-ins. Decision 6's trigger is 'the attempt's units hold a first-pass row and the verdict is unplaced', and Decision 1 makes a unit naming more than one change unplaced. The eject path covers only 'a refusal whose every row names one change'. As written, this refusal therefore stops the runner and ejects nothing, and the stop message says 'naming no change of the batch', which is false here.
decisions.why: This is an exception to 'ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands', and the block gives it no argument of its own. Neither of Decision 6's two justifications holds for it. A change did fail: the row names it. Nothing says its repair would be refused again, since the same kind of row naming ONE change is ejected as red. Applying the rule is not impossible here, because the failing changes are named. The only way into this case is the mechanism's wording, not a reason. It is a wrong outcome: the runner stops a batch it could handle, wakes the coordinator with a false message, and lands nothing. What the plan should say instead: a first-pass row naming several changes of the batch ejects those named changes (as red, or as one entry like Decision 1's), and the rest is run again. The stop, and the 'naming no change' message, are limited to refusals whose rows name no change of the batch (6b) or that also carry such a row (6d). Pin it with a test of a two-change row.

decisions.summary: A first-pass refusal in which one row names a change of the batch and another row names none (a hold or lock of no batch task). As written it is unplaced, so it stops the runner with nothing ejected.
decisions.why: Judged separately from 6c. The row that names no change of the batch blocks the rest of the batch whatever is ejected, and would refuse the repairs too, so 'the rest of the batch lands' cannot be reached while it holds. Nothing is lost: on resume, once the hold clears, the named change's row refuses again and is ejected by the rule. The plan should state this case explicitly, and its stop message should not say 'naming no change' when a row names one.

decisions.summary: A kill between filing a repair entry and writing its eject lines resumes as a new attempt. An entry is a change's repair only where an eject line names it, and T16's queue reads by that rule. Finishing the interrupted ejection at resume is priced and not taken.
decisions.why: This is crash-recovery mechanism. With the rule that an entry is a change's repair only where an eject line names it, a change the resumed attempt lands is never returned as a repair, so the request's 'the ejected task returns to the queue as a repair entry' holds exactly for the changes actually ejected. The cost is stated and handed to T16 explicitly.

decisions.summary: T20's wake::dead rule is revisited: only the runner's own stopped:true line tells a death, not any owed line of the open batch.
decisions.why: It fixes a wrong outcome: since T15, an owed line no longer means the runner stopped, so a runner killed in a later attempt was never reported to the coordinator. Restoring a wake the design already owes widens nothing. The wake itself is the death case of 6a and 6b, and FR-005's 'US5's cases' could not be checked because US5 is not in the bundle.

decisions.summary: The attribution reads a check's Phase line where the gate's writer files it: the pool-holder chain and feature_of through the SPECIFY_FEATURE that make land exports. The real lane-tree line is left to T23 to observe.
decisions.why: This is where the gate's own record is read, as FR-004's attribute step requires. It is pinned by a test with the real writer. Saying that no lane-tree line exists yet, and handing its measurement to T23, is honest scoping and takes nothing out of the request.

decisions.summary: One owed line per repair entry, naming the entry, its units and the attempt file. One attempt's lines are written together, so one lane-wait returns them as one wake.
decisions.why: FR-005 says 'once per landed batch ... otherwise only for US5's cases'. A red attempt's owed lines are a wake that is not per landed batch, and US5's text is not in the bundle, so how it fits FR-005 is not confirmed here. On the request it is within: the sketch gives the coordinator dispatching ('I'd dispatch, read short reports'), and the ejected task 'returns to the queue as a repair entry' for a fresh builder. Telling the coordinator, in one wake per attempt, that there are repairs to dispatch is that role, and integration work stays out of its context (SC-004). It narrows nothing the GM asked for. The block labels the fresh-builder route D7's; D7 is not in the bundle.

decisions.summary: The suite and row readers read the attempt file, which make land's inherited stdout and stderr go to. The --src hooks Phase lines stay an unbuilt fallback.
decisions.why: This is a measured reading of where the output actually lands, with the code paths named. It chooses where to read the gate's own record and changes nothing in scope.

### T15 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Phase 2: a red unit naming no change or several, or no unit read, ejects the batch as one 'unplaced' entry; phase 3 (T24) replaces attribute() with D6's halving.
decisions.why: This is the order the work is built in, not a carve-out from it. FR-004 ('attribute, else bisect') and the request's 'bisects and ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands' are met by phases 2 and 3 together, and the block names the task that replaces this route. It would be a narrowing only if T24 were dropped or the feature closed without it. Ejecting the batch as one repair entry for a fresh builder still keeps the coordinator out of the repair (SC-003).

decisions.summary: A crate is its directory, its dependents are not counted; a change to core that reddens lane's tests is unplaced and phase 3's halving places it.
decisions.why: D6's own wording. A case it cannot place falls to Decision 1 and then to the bisect the request asks for. It narrows no outcome.

decisions.summary: A Phase line naming several crates is one unit over all of them; only its printed form is cut, with a NAMED knob.
decisions.why: A defect fix: reading a family cover-build one crate at a time ejected an innocent change, which is the opposite of 'ejects the failing change'. The display knob is only the owed line's length and changes no outcome.

decisions.summary: A hook suite maps to a delta path by its guard file name and the guard sources, the shared crate included.
decisions.why: How D6's map is carried out. It decides how a failing change is found and drops nothing the request asked for.

decisions.summary: A first-pass row maps by a delta path in its text or by its leading task list.
decisions.why: How D6's 'a row by its file' is carried out, with the first pass's own form used. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Exit -1, or a first-pass refusal with a row naming no change of the batch (a hold, a lock, an owed round of no task in it), ejects nothing: the runner stops with the batch open and a stopped owed line, and lane-start resumes it. A row naming one change ejects that change; a row naming several ejects them as one entry, and the rest runs again.
decisions.why: This narrows 'on a red result it ... ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands': in two cases nothing is ejected and nothing lands. Taken one case at a time. (a) Exit -1: make did not start or was killed, so no change failed and there is no 'failing change' to eject. Ejecting on no evidence would eject innocent changes and defeat the request's purpose, which is that only the failing change leaves. (b) A refusal naming no change of the batch: no change of the batch caused it, and while the hold stands it refuses every first pass, the rest of the batch and every repair included. Landing the rest is physically impossible until it clears. (c) A row naming no change next to a row naming one: the hold still refuses any landing, so the named change being ejected on the resume rather than now loses nothing. The coordinator hears of the stop through the stopped line (Decision 8), so the stop is not silent. Rows that do name changes eject only those changes, and the rest lands, as asked.

decisions.summary: A kill between filing an entry and its eject lines resumes as a new attempt; an entry is a change's repair only where an eject line names it; entries are filed once per batch and set.
decisions.why: Crash recovery inside the red path. The cost it names, an entry's 'ejected' list naming a change that later lands, produces no wrong outcome, because T16 reads a repair from the eject lines. Nothing the request asked for is cut.

decisions.summary: Only the runner's own stopped line tells a death; an ejection's owed line no longer counts as one.
decisions.why: A defect fix, shown red first: a runner killed after an ejection was never reported to the coordinator. It now reports more deaths, not fewer.

decisions.why: A make that never ran, or was killed, gives no evidence against the change being carried. Ejecting on it would send innocent changes to repair, which defeats the request's 'ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands'. This is T15 Decision 6's ruled case for make land's exit -1, applied to the carry.

decisions.summary: A carry that ran and failed on one named change with no unmerged path (Decision 4's 'a carry whose verified end failed') also stops the runner with the batch open, nothing ejected
decisions.why: The ground given, 'no conflict names a change', is word-level. Each make carry COMMIT= is a carry of one named change, so a carry of it that ran and failed is evidence on that change in a way exit -1 is not. Stopping leaves the batch open and the next lane-start re-carries the same change and stops again. That is the wrong outcome the block's own item 12 says T25 removes ('every later start re-stopping on it ... a batch's innocent changes waited on the coordinator's hand'), and it goes against the GM's 'the rest of the batch lands' and FR-005/SC-001. T15 Decision 6, which the block cites, does the opposite for make land: only exit -1 and a refusal naming no change stop; every other non-zero exit is a red and ejects. The bundle does not say what the carry's 'verified end' checks, and the block gives no evidence that such a failure is the tooling's rather than the change's. Its pin is only a carry-fails stand-in. Fix: a carry of one change that exits non-zero, not -1, with no unmerged path ejects that change as a repair entry (integrate, its carry log as attempt, units none or the verified-end's output) and the batch goes on. Keep the stop only where the failure is shown to be the lane's own, for example the same failure on every carry of the set, and state that evidence in the label. Or restate the decision with the measured reason a verified-end failure cannot be the change's.

decisions.summary: A carry that fails with no unmerged path ejects its change (why carry). Only the lane's own tree's stops still stop the runner with the batch open and nothing ejected: exit -1, and the carry's refusal of unfinished work in the lane's tree (CARRY_REFUSED).
decisions.why: The request reads 'ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands'. That answers round 1's 4b objection. Only two cases are kept as stops, and each was judged on its own. (a) Exit -1, where make could not start or was killed: no change is named, so there is no failing change to eject. Ejecting would remove an innocent change on no evidence, which defeats the rule's purpose of landing the innocent rest. (b) CARRY_REFUSED: the carry refuses unfinished work in the lane's own tree before it touches the change, so every change of the batch would be refused alike. decisions.summary: A conflict inside a halving's set ends the halving. The survivors land or go red as a plain attempt (a red unplaced starts a fresh halving), and the rest of the batch runs as one.
decisions.why: The request's bisect, eject and land-the-rest all still happen: a red among the survivors starts a fresh halving, and the failing change is still ejected while the rest lands. US4's bound, which SC-003 cites, is stated for one bad change. A conflict ejection during a halving is a second faulty change that the bound does not describe. The extra runs are a cost, not a fidelity finding, and the decision drops nothing that was asked.
