decisions.summary: An entry that waits= on another task still waits for that task's carry (the waits closure's uncarried test unchanged).
decisions.why: Not a carve-out from the change: the removed wait was needless only because the entry's own handout builds on the commit; a waits= entry's tree does not, so its wait still guards something. Keeping it narrows nothing the GM or the spec asked.

decisions.summary: The built state's text ('the carry of <task>'s done commit owed') and make builder-trees' listing are unchanged.
decisions.why: The build half's entry does still owe its carry; the wording stays true. Nothing asked is left undone.

decisions.summary: Change confined to the guard's shared crate; make builder-next, builder-done's next-dispatch line and the pool-idle Stop guard change through shared::builder_queue (next, idle); no gate or guard file edited; module doc item 5 restated.
decisions.why: Implementation placement; consistent with FR-008 (no check dropped) and with the goal stated in part A item 1.

decisions.summary: Two tests pin the behavior (closing half READY with T1 uncarried while a waits=T1 entry still waits; a real-clone idle test); exits are builder-checks for shared and guard plus the pool-idle hook suite.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the decided behavior, carrying one-shot labels on every figure (17/2 red, 19 after, 603/629/33 passed). Verification of what was asked, not new scope.

decisions.summary: The second-red tripwire (second_red_gate in make done) stands down for the lane's own runs only (D6 step 4); every other run meets it as before.
decisions.why: The lane's red handling is the request's own item 1 and FR-004 (attribute, bisect, eject, land the rest, file a repair); the gate and push checks still run on every lane attempt and a red still lands nothing, so FR-008 (a change lands only through the same gate and push checks) is untouched. The tripwire governs what a session must do after a second red, not whether a change passes the gate.

decisions.summary: The lane's tree is required on the runner branch too, not only on the open-batch branch: (variable AND lane tree) AND (batch open OR runner-started).
decisions.why: Stricter than D6's literal grouping: it narrows the stand-down (a carve-out from the tripwire), keeping more runs under the tripwire; it narrows nothing the GM asked for, and costs the lane nothing since every attempt runs in its tree (D1).

decisions.summary: L7R_LANE_BATCH is required on every branch and is never sufficient alone.
decisions.why: Keeps the variable from being an unrecorded escape (a by-hand make land with it exported still owes the arbiter); serves FR-008.

decisions.summary: batch_open re-reads l7r-lane/lane.jsonl in the tree crate (mirroring the lane's Batch::open, torn lines skipped) rather than depending on the lane crate, to avoid a crate cycle; runner_started probes lane.lock with flock -n and walks /proc ancestry.
decisions.why: Implementation choice of how to test D6's conditions; changes no requested behavior.

decisions.summary: Ten state tests, red first against a stub lane_run (3 failed, 7 passed as the unchanged cases must), then 10 of 10 green and builder-checks clean.
decisions.why: Tests that enforce the requested stand-down and that every other run is still stopped; enforcement of what was asked, not added scope.

decisions.summary: The lock is the truth, the pid secondary: the starter probes, spawns and waits for the runner to take the lock; a racing second runner loses flock -n and exits 0.
decisions.why: Mechanism of FR-003's lane running in its own process; settles nothing the request or spec decides and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The runner's start and stop lines name no batch, so a NOW=1 kill mid-batch leaves the batch resumable under T11's state_of.
decisions.why: Implementation of resumability (survive a kill by its log); keeps a batch from being lost, which serves FR-003/FR-004 rather than narrowing them.

decisions.summary: A stop request is keyed by pid; one naming another pid is dropped at the next runner's start.
decisions.why: Correctness of the stop verb; no requested behavior is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The idle clock runs from the newest NEW hand-in or batch run, never from 'nothing waiting'; LANE_IDLE_S 3600 s labeled GUESS.
decisions.why: Implementation detail of the runner's idle stop; the request and spec set no idle rule, and the knob is labeled as a guess.

decisions.summary: Recovery names the open batch and hands resume its remaining changes; bringing the tree to origin/main and running the rest is T14's seam, the batch left open until then.
decisions.why: A task split within the plan; the open batch is left open (not dropped or landed differently), so nothing of FR-003/FR-004 is cut, only sequenced to T14.

decisions.summary: A hand-in starts the runner only from phase 2's base (HAND_IN_BASE=origin); in phase 1 on_hand_in passes through, T22 flips the base and switches it on.
decisions.why: In phase 1 it defers part of what was asked: FR-003's lane taking hand-ins from the done refs, and SC-001's batch run with no coordinator turn between the hand-ins and the push, do not start from a hand-in until T22 flips the base (it also narrows the plan's D2, 'every hand-in'). LEGITIMATE on the purpose ground: in phase 1 the coordinator lands by hand, so a runner started by each hand-in and batching the same hand-ins would race it - two landers of one change, which defeats FR-003/FR-008's single route through the same gate and push rather than serving them. The deferral is bounded: T22 switches it on with no further edit, and the 'For T22' note pins the single-point flip and a test with the variable unset. The start's failure never changes the hand-in's exit, so no existing check is touched. (D2 and D3 are not in the bundle; their content is taken from this block's own account.)

decisions.summary: The stall watchdog exempts only a session whose own backgrounded 'l7r-gate lane wait' (descending from its registry pid) runs while the clone's runner lives; other sessions of the clone are judged as before; inert until T20 adds the wait.
decisions.why: It narrows an existing guard's reach, which the request did not ask to preserve; it is implied by the request itself - the GM approved a thin coordinator that dispatches and reads short reports, and FR-005 lets the lane wake the coordinator once per landed batch and otherwise only for US5's cases, so a stall nudge on a coordinator deliberately waiting on the lane (D9, per this block's account; D9 is not in the bundle) is a wake the spec forbids. By the block's own account, the earlier forms (the runner alone exempting every session; a clone-wide wait) were ruled NOT LEGITIMATE; this form exempts exactly the session doing the waiting, for exactly the life of its wait while the runner lives, and is tested to judge a second session of the clone. Bound if the lane hangs while the session waits: the LONG_RUN warning still fires in this block, so a hung wait is not silent; T47's removal of that warning is T47's to justify at its own review. FR-008 is not touched: the watchdog is not a gate or push check.

decisions.summary: Timing knobs POLL_S 5 s, START_WAIT_S 5 s, STOP_WAIT_S 10 s, TAKE_S 1 s labeled GUESS and audited; LANE_IDLE_S and LANE_POLL_S read from the environment, a non-number refused.
decisions.why: Implementation constants, each labeled as a guess; nothing requested is narrowed.

decisions.id: T12 Approach - the work loop's endings
decisions.summary: The work loop ends on its own stop request, on LANE_IDLE_S idle ('stop why idle'), or on a failing step or resume ('stop why error: <e>'); at start it writes 'start {pid, why}' and resumes the log's last open batch.
decisions.why: How the detached runner (D2) ends and records it; an error stop leaves the batch's log for Recovery rather than landing or dropping work, so nothing of FR-003/FR-004 is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The runner takes its lock with a bounded retry (flock_within TAKE_S), closing a start race; measured 200 of 200 cycles started, 0 runners left.
decisions.why: A correctness fix inside the runner's mechanism; carries a dated, method-labeled measurement.

decisions.summary: T22 must flip HAND_IN_BASE in one place (one public reading in the land crate that land_or_hand_in asks), tested with the variable unset; written on T22's line.
decisions.why: A constraint placed on a later task so that Decision 6's phase-1 limit cannot outlive phase 1; it protects the requested end state rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: A hand-in-started runner inherits the caller's binary and environment (T, F, L7R_GATE_TREE); T14, the first to run make land from the runner, clears them and runs the lane tree's l7r-gate; dormant until then.
decisions.why: A latent issue that cannot occur before T14 (the runner runs no make land yet and is started only by make lane-start before T22), assigned to the task where it would first matter; this keeps FR-003's 'existing make land checks there' honest rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: The watchdog's 1800 s long-run warning would nudge a coordinator waiting on make lane-wait past 30 minutes; not fixed here, filed as T47 to land with T20 and before T22.
decisions.why: Not a defect carried forward: make lane-wait is T20's command and does not exist, so the wake FR-005 forbids cannot happen until T20, and T47 is scheduled to land with T20 and before T22 so no coordinator waits on the lane without it. Leaving it to that task neither narrows FR-005 nor carries a live defect into a step where it manifests.

decisions.summary: shared::builder_pool gains pools_all (every clone's registry read whole via read_all, the lane's tree included) beside pools (read, builders only), both through one private across; builder_pool_hooks::refusal protects pools_all, so a hand worktree remove/move/rm of <clone>-land or rm of its warm cache is refused
decisions.why: Enforces D1 (the lane's tree kept, its cache warm), which serves FR-003 (the lane runs in its own worktree) and the request's item 1; a guard that blocks only hand removal of the exact tree and cache the lane needs is enforcement of what was asked, with no reach to other agents, commands or defaults.

decisions.summary: builder_brief_hooks and workflow_hooks keep reading pools, so every count of builders' trees still leaves the lane out
decisions.why: Leaves the brief and Workflow verdicts as they are; the lane is not a builder's tree, so including it there would change behavior nobody asked to change. Search space stated (grep -rn "pools(" rust, three callers, each judged).

decisions.summary: Membership stays the registry: a -land tree no clone's registry names still passes
decisions.why: The lane's tree is registered (T13, Tree::lane), so it is protected; an unregistered tree that merely has the name's shape is not the lane's tree, and keeping membership on the registry follows the standing rule (451 T285). Nothing the request or D1 asks for is cut.

decisions.summary: The refusal reuses the guard's existing REMOVE message unchanged
decisions.why: No new behavior or wording; the same escape as for a builder's tree.

decisions.summary: The REMOVE message's make builder-tree-drop is a dead end for the held lane tree (drop_tree refuses held trees, T13 refuses releasing lane); not fixed here, filed as T49, landing before T22, BUILDER_TREE_OK escape meanwhile
decisions.why: A real defect, but it is scheduled inside this feature as its own task and lands before the next dependent task (T22), so it is not carried into the next step; the escape keeps the lane's tree removable in the interim. Splitting a gate crate's command out of a guard brief narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: drop_tree takes the lane's tree (held by builder_pool::LANE): refused while the lane's runner lives (lane.lock held, flock -n probe, names make lane-stop) or a batch of lane.jsonl is open (names the batch and make lane-start); otherwise removed as any free tree is (REASON owed, worktree, cache and registry line gone, drop logged) and adoptable again; no BUILDER_TREE_OK escape.
decisions.why: Tooling for the lane's own worktree (FR-003: the lane runs in its own worktree). It adds a safe route to retire that tree and keeps the refusals the task's brief names (runner alive, batch open). It removes no check (FR-008) and narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The open-batch test follows the lane's own grouping (log::batches/state_of): a batch line opens, landed/stop end, carry/eject/run/attribute/push reopen, batch-less stop and torn lines change nothing. It is read privately in the task crate, not by depending on the lane crate or making tree's helpers public.
decisions.why: An implementation choice about how to read whether a batch is open. It matches the lane's semantics and is forced by crate dependency direction. The request and spec do not settle it, and it narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Every other builder tree's rules and the not-free branch's message are unchanged. No guard-rendered message changes, because the REMOVE message (T45) already names make builder-tree-drop.
decisions.why: Keeps existing behavior outside the lane's tree. Nothing is narrowed or added beyond the task.

decisions.summary: A lane tree gone from disk mid-batch is still a dead end: the gone-from-disk refusal names the drop, which stays refused while the runner lives or a batch is open. Not fixed here: filed as T50, to land before T22.
decisions.why: Fixing it here would contradict this task's own brief (refuse the drop while a batch is open), and it needs a separate route decision. The defect is not left unfixed or carried past the next step: it is filed as T50 and ordered to land before T22, as fix-as-we-go requires. That defers a defect to a scheduled task rather than narrowing the request.

decisions.summary: lane_start, finding the registry's lane tree gone from disk, prunes and re-makes the worktree at the registry's path from the clone's HEAD, logs a remake line, and falls through to the usual fetch/reset/clean/detach at origin/main, instead of refusing with the drop T49 now refuses.
decisions.why: Serves FR-003 (the lane runs in its own worktree) and the request's purpose that the lane run without coordinator turns or hand steps (sketch item 1, FR-005/SC-001): a dead end that needs a hand step is the failure being fixed. It drops no check (FR-008): the tree is reset to origin/main exactly as before, so the batch's gate and push are unchanged.

decisions.summary: Does not write a stop of the open batch from the task crate (the brief's example), to avoid a second writer of l7r-lane/lane.jsonl beside the lane crate's own.
decisions.why: A design choice between two routes to the same end. It leaves nothing the request or spec asks for undone: the batch carries on, which is more of what was asked than stopping it.

decisions.summary: The re-made tree keeps its build cache (builder_pool::cache keyed by the tree's name); D1's rule against making the lane's tree is held not to apply to one re-made at the same path.
decisions.why: Keeps D1's own purpose (a new tree starts cold) rather than excepting it: the re-made tree is warm where the cache survived. Nothing the GM asked is narrowed; FR-006's token and throughput goal is served, not cut.

decisions.summary: T13's 'refused, never made' stands for a lane tree never adopted; only the gone-from-disk case changes.
decisions.why: Bounds the fix to the found-and-left defect T49 named. Nothing in request.md or the spec index requires the lane to make a never-adopted tree, and the never-adopted refusal is not a dead end the block reports, so no known defect is carried forward.

decisions.summary: When git cannot make the tree because something stands at the path, the refusal names what is in the way and the git worktree add's message, no longer the drop; the next batch start makes it once the path is clear.
decisions.why: Replaces a refusal that sent the session to a refused command with one that names the actual obstruction. That serves FR-002's own standard that a refusal names its fix, and it narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: The builders' own gone-from-disk note (take's, naming the drop) is left as it is, as is the drop (T49), and no lane-crate edit is made.
decisions.why: A free builder tree is one the drop takes. T49's refusal covers only the lane tree while the runner lives or a batch is open, so the builders' note is not the dead end and leaving it unchanged leaves no defect. Not touching the lane crate leaves nothing of the request undone.

decisions.summary: Under L7R_LANE_BATCH, carry_done keeps only done commits whose sha matches a change the batch's batch line names (full or short prefix); the rest are left with their refs kept and named on one 'left' line for a later batch.
decisions.why: Carries D14 (a batch takes its changes' shas when it forms; a later hand-in changes no open batch) for FR-003's lane, which takes hand-ins from the done refs; nothing is dropped - the left commits keep their refs and land in the next batch through the same gate (FR-008).

decisions.summary: The LAST batch line naming the batch is read; a torn line is skipped, as the lane's log::batches does.
decisions.why: Reads the batch the same way the lane writes and reads it; settles nothing the request or spec asked otherwise.

decisions.summary: A landed line for the batch after its batch line ends the filter: a by-hand make land with a finished batch's id exported carries as before.
decisions.why: Keeps a landing outside the lane unchanged and never leaves a task's commits uncarried; FR-008 (nothing of the existing landing dropped). Restores existing behavior only where no lane batch is open, so it narrows no requested behavior.

decisions.id: T52-4 stop does not end it
decisions.summary: A stop line naming the batch does not end the filter (the lane resumes the batch), so T17's landed|stop rule is not copied.
decisions.why: Keeps D14 holding over a resumed batch's whole window; widens, not narrows, the requirement's reach.

decisions.id: T52-5 private reader in land crate
decisions.summary: The log is read by a small private reader in the land crate, not through the lane crate and not by making T17's state::batch_open public.
decisions.why: A placement and structure choice inside T17's rule (log read in the land crate without the lane crate); not a fidelity matter.

decisions.summary: Of the brief's two fixes ('carries nothing' or 'only the batch line's shas'), the second.
decisions.why: Both options were the brief's; the chosen one holds D14 whether or not the lane carried first and keeps make land's carry verifying a batch's commit is in HEAD, so no existing check is dropped (FR-008).

decisions.summary: A batch id no batch line names, or the variable unset, carries as before.
decisions.why: The lane writes the batch line before make land (runner/run.rs, read 2026-11-27), so inside the lane every batch is named; the fallback is the unchanged landing outside the lane, which the brief and FR-008 require.

decisions.summary: Measured done is the red-then-green tests now; in use, the lane's first real batch (T23) with a later hand-in left waiting and its left line in the attempt file.
decisions.why: A verification schedule for the requested behavior; defers no requested part and leaves no known defect (Found and left: none).

decisions.summary: Restate the ## help lines of builder-tree-adopt, builder-tree-drop and builder-trees in the root Makefile (via make guard-edit) to describe the lane's tree as T13/T49/T50 built it, and regenerate docs/make-targets.html with make docs
decisions.why: Documents the landing lane's own worktree (FR-003, the GM's 'a landing lane of its own ... in its own worktree' sketch item 1) as already built; adds no behavior and narrows nothing the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: No code changes; the lines are restated to what builder_tree.rs does now, read 2026-11-27
decisions.why: A documentation-only correction of a found-and-left gap; the code's behavior is the spec's, and leaving it unchanged removes nothing asked for.

decisions.summary: No red-first test, since no test pins the help lines' words (grep of tests/ and rust/ for the three target names, 2026-11-27, search space stated)
decisions.why: Not adding a test for help text drops no requested behavior or check (FR-008 concerns the gate and push checks, untouched); the exit is make docs reporting 0 undocumented.

decisions.summary: Runs after T12, T13, T49 and T50 (T12 holds the Makefile) and before T22
decisions.why: Sequencing only; describes the lane after its parts land, narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: one mark reader (take_unread/unread) in l7r_shared::lane_wake, shared by make lane-wait and the prompt hook
decisions.why: Where the code lives is an implementation choice. Having one rule for what counts as unread is how FR-005's once-per-line wake is met. Nothing asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: whichever reader comes first (wait or prompt hook) moves the mark, serialized by the mark's lock
decisions.why: It serves FR-005 directly. A hook that printed without moving the mark would make the re-armed wait wake again on a line already shown, which is a wake FR-005 does not list.

decisions.summary: the wait writes one runner-dead owed line when no runner holds the lock over an open last batch for DEAD_GRACE_S
decisions.why: This is a new kind of wake. FR-005 allows wakes only for US5's cases, and US5's text is not in the bundle, so whether US5 names a dead runner could not be checked. It is still not a narrowing: without it a stranded batch would block the coordinator's wait for ever with nothing coming (a hang), and the GM's sketch keeps for the coordinator exactly 'the rare case that needs judgment'. It stays quiet in the cases that need no one (an idle end, a lane-stop after a landing, phase 1's hand-ins landed by hand).

decisions.summary: the prompt hook prints unread lane lines before solo::alone's only-session return
decisions.why: A coordinator whose builders are subagents is the only session. Returning before printing would drop the lines for the session FR-005 says they are owed to.

decisions.summary: a flagless verb with its knobs from the environment, matching T12's waits_on_lane argv; WAIT_POLL_S 5 s, DEAD_GRACE_S 30 s, LOCK_S 5 s labeled GUESS and audited; no ceiling
decisions.why: Wiring and new constants, labeled GUESS and audited. Having no ceiling follows D9. Nothing asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: wake::dead treats any owed line naming the open batch since the last start as having already told the death, so one red run wakes once
decisions.why: It narrows when Decision 3 reports a death: no runner-dead line is written if an owed line already names the open batch. That is FR-005's own limit. Under T14's red stand-in, the red line already says the runner stopped and the batch is open, so a second wake for the same red is one FR-005 does not list. Round 3 ruled accepting that double wake NOT LEGITIMATE, and this decision removes it. A new start followed by a kill is still reported. Caveat: the rule is phrased wider than its reason, since any owed line naming the open batch counts. That is sound only while the red line is the one owed line that can name a still-open batch. T15, which changes the red path, has to revisit it.

decisions.summary: T47 (the watchdog exemption) and T21 (the Stop rule keeping the wait armed, with its own l7r_shared reading) left to their own filed tasks
decisions.why: Work is split across tasks that are already filed. Nothing asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: a WAITING hand-in with no runner serving it is not called dead (only an open batch is); deferred to T56, which lands with T22 before T23
decisions.why: In phase 2 this is a hang, so it is a defect. It is not live in phase 1: such hand-ins are landed by hand there, and staying quiet is correct, because calling them dead would add wakes FR-005 does not list. The defect only appears once T22 flips the base. The block files T56 to land with T22, before T23 runs the real batch. Legitimate on that ordering condition: T56 must land no later than T22.

decisions.summary: A measurement script under dev/measurements reuses T02's night-figures.py for landings, pool replay and load, so after figures count as the night's did; no engine or tooling change.
decisions.why: SC-002 and FR-010 ask for after figures comparable with the night's; reusing T02's counting rule is what makes them comparable. Changes nothing the spec settles.

decisions.summary: Measures over 19:57Z-23:03Z (3.11 h, after T08/T43) and 21:06Z-23:03Z (after T44), states trees held and load beside each against the night's 3.19 and 14.1, and says outright the window is not a LIKE window and seven attempts agree with SC-002's 'well under' without establishing it.
decisions.why: FR-010 requires every before-and-after figure beside both windows' concurrency; the block does that and does not declare SC-002 met on a short, unlike window, leaving the like-window reading to T31, so nothing asked is narrowed. One note, not a ruling: the block's night baseline is T02's record (17 of 39, beside the 3.19 trees held of FR-010's 04:30Z-14:29Z window) while SC-002 names 19 of 50; 0 of 7 is under either, and results.md should say which window each night figure is over.

decisions.summary: Records hand-ins, refusals at hand-in by cause, whether each refusal named its fixing command, who resolved conflicts, and that no hand-in ran coverage.
decisions.why: Each figure is a clause of SC-002 (refused at hand-in with its fixing command, runs no coverage) or of the sketch's item 2 (conflicts fixed by the builder with the context).

decisions.summary: Names what the event and pool logs cannot show (exit codes, refused or conflicted hand-ins) and fills it from the subagent transcripts as a labeled second source.
decisions.why: Serves the measurement SC-002 asks for; a stated gap filled by a labeled source, not a scope change.

decisions.summary: This task's own hand-in is reported in the builder's report because the committed record cannot hold its outcome.
decisions.why: A reporting placement; changes nothing asked.

decisions.summary: The likeness test counts the lane's own worktree as a held builder tree (3.55 vs 2.94); T10's own figures exclude it, and the tooling fix is filed as T59, landing before T31.
decisions.why: Not a narrowing: T10's figures are already corrected for it, and the fix is in the feature's own task list ordered before the like-window measurement it would distort, so no known defect is carried into the step it affects.

decisions.summary: A build half's hand-in is refused for the feature-close ask only its closing half can answer (a check refusing correct work); filed as T60, landing before T31.
decisions.why: A defect, and it is not left: it is filed in this feature and ordered before T31, the next step whose figures it would affect. A measurement task changing no tooling is the task's own stated scope, not a cut to what the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Green/red exits (red through make arbiter-ask), one-landing budget, tagged performance work as a measurement under 451 FR-013.
decisions.why: 451 FR-013 counts measurement of where the time goes as performance work; exits and budget decide nothing the spec left open in a way that narrows it.

decisions.summary: Phase 2: a red unit naming no change or several, or no unit read, ejects the batch as one 'unplaced' entry; phase 3 (T24) replaces attribute() with D6's halving.
decisions.why: This is the order the work is built in, not a carve-out from it. FR-004 ('attribute, else bisect') and the request's 'bisects and ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands' are met by phases 2 and 3 together, and the block names the task that replaces this route. It would be a narrowing only if T24 were dropped or the feature closed without it. Ejecting the batch as one repair entry for a fresh builder still keeps the coordinator out of the repair (SC-003).

decisions.summary: A crate is its directory, its dependents are not counted; a change to core that reddens lane's tests is unplaced and phase 3's halving places it.
decisions.why: D6's own wording. A case it cannot place falls to Decision 1 and then to the bisect the request asks for. It narrows no outcome.

decisions.summary: A Phase line naming several crates is one unit over all of them; only its printed form is cut, with a NAMED knob.
decisions.why: A defect fix: reading a family cover-build one crate at a time ejected an innocent change, which is the opposite of 'ejects the failing change'. The display knob is only the owed line's length and changes no outcome.

decisions.summary: A hook suite maps to a delta path by its guard file name and the guard sources, the shared crate included.
decisions.why: How D6's map is carried out. It decides how a failing change is found and drops nothing the request asked for.

decisions.summary: A first-pass row maps by a delta path in its text or by its leading task list.
decisions.why: How D6's 'a row by its file' is carried out, with the first pass's own form used. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Exit -1, or a first-pass refusal with a row naming no change of the batch (a hold, a lock, an owed round of no task in it), ejects nothing: the runner stops with the batch open and a stopped owed line, and lane-start resumes it. A row naming one change ejects that change; a row naming several ejects them as one entry, and the rest runs again.
decisions.why: This narrows 'on a red result it ... ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands': in two cases nothing is ejected and nothing lands. Taken one case at a time. (a) Exit -1: make did not start or was killed, so no change failed and there is no 'failing change' to eject. Ejecting on no evidence would eject innocent changes and defeat the request's purpose, which is that only the failing change leaves. (b) A refusal naming no change of the batch: no change of the batch caused it, and while the hold stands it refuses every first pass, the rest of the batch and every repair included. Landing the rest is physically impossible until it clears. (c) A row naming no change next to a row naming one: the hold still refuses any landing, so the named change being ejected on the resume rather than now loses nothing. The coordinator hears of the stop through the stopped line (Decision 8), so the stop is not silent. Rows that do name changes eject only those changes, and the rest lands, as asked.

decisions.summary: A kill between filing an entry and its eject lines resumes as a new attempt; an entry is a change's repair only where an eject line names it; entries are filed once per batch and set.
decisions.why: Crash recovery inside the red path. The cost it names, an entry's 'ejected' list naming a change that later lands, produces no wrong outcome, because T16 reads a repair from the eject lines. Nothing the request asked for is cut.

decisions.summary: Only the runner's own stopped line tells a death; an ejection's owed line no longer counts as one.
decisions.why: A defect fix, shown red first: a runner killed after an ejection was never reported to the coordinator. It now reports more deaths, not fewer.

decisions.summary: The attribution reads a check's Phase line where the gate's writer files it, through the pool holder and feature_of, under the runner's SPECIFY_FEATURE.
decisions.why: Where the gate's own record is read from. It decides no scope, and a test pins it.

decisions.summary: One owed line per repair entry; one attempt's lines are written together, so one lane-wait returns them as one wake.
decisions.why: Each line is a dispatch the coordinator owes (a fresh builder per D7). That is the 'I'd dispatch, read short reports' of the sketch the GM called 'very sensible', not integration work. Grouping an attempt's lines into one wake keeps wakes few, in line with FR-005.

decisions.summary: The suite and row readers read the attempt file, which make land's stdout and stderr go to; the --src hooks Phase lines stay an unbuilt fallback.
decisions.why: Which record the attribution reads, measured by reading the code. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: An open repair is offered before every queue entry, a performance entry's included (LANE_REPAIR_FIRST=1; 0 offers it only where no queue entry is picked); unwritten performance lines stay first in builder-done's step 1 and the Stop block
decisions.why: The request's sketch item 1 has the ejected task 'return to the queue as a repair entry' and FR-004/SC-003 have it go to a fresh builder; neither sets its order against other entries. Ordering it first delays nothing the GM asked for, and the knob's 0 still offers it. A priority choice inside what was asked.

decisions.summary: Open is read from the lane's eject lines (an entry is offered only once an eject line names it; its changes and tasks from those lines), never from the repair entry alone
decisions.why: Implements FR-004's 'eject ... file the repair' as the data model defines a repair entry; it narrows nothing the request or spec names - an entry no eject names is not an ejected change.

decisions.summary: A repair is closed by a done line naming it in repair_of, or superseded by a later hand-in of its feature sharing a task
decisions.why: The repair exists to land the ejected task's change (sketch item 1, US4); a later hand-in of that task after the eject is the change being handed in again, so offering the stale repair would dispatch a second builder for work already answered. The data model's 'superseded' reading; earlier hand-ins, undone hand-ins and other features' tasks do not close it.

decisions.summary: Passed over with a line: a repair whose task is in flight in a pool tree, and an integrate-kind repair no make builder-brief takes (until T19)
decisions.why: In flight: offering it would hand the tree back to its holder, which US4 ('no builder is kept past its report') forbids - the pass-over enforces the request. Integrate: the sketch's item 3 and US5/SC-004 route integration work to a fresh agent, not a builder brief, so offering a builder-brief command that refuses would serve nothing; the entry is still named on a line, so nothing is hidden or dropped.

decisions.summary: REPAIR= passes the brief's mechanism refusal, and is itself refused before any tree is taken where no open entry has the id or the entry's feature, tasks or kind are not the brief's
decisions.why: FR-008's 'nothing dropped' is the landing's gate and push checks, which a repair still passes in full; the brief-time refusal was already met when the line was first briefed and built, and the repair is one fix of that same line (US4). The REPAIR= refusals add a check rather than remove one. No clause of the request or spec is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The handout's base is the clone's HEAD until T22 moves it to origin/main (D13)
decisions.why: Phasing of a base the plan's D3/D13 already settle; the request and spec set no base for a repair handout, and the move is scheduled, not dropped.

decisions.summary: The knob is read by the commands and handed in (run_with, dispatch_with) so the task crate's tests run both ways
decisions.why: Test plumbing; touches no clause of the request or spec.

decisions.summary: A fresh builder, never one kept past its report: the queue never offers a repair in flight, and the command's line and the brief's REPAIR line say FRESH
decisions.why: Directly implements US4 and SC-003 ('the failing change returned as a repair for a fresh builder') and the sketch's item 3 (the coordinator does not repair).

decisions.summary: This closes 451 T308's two-tier split: first tier the builder's (T06-T08), full gate the lane's (T14), 'repaired by whoever is cheapest' replaced by a fresh builder on a repair entry, builder coverage by none
decisions.why: The GM's first message is that the second tier was meant not to block; moving the full gate into the lane and repairs to fresh builders is the sketch's items 1-3. 'Builder coverage by none' follows the spec's recorded striking of 'coverage for its own crates' (request.md, spec-fidelity 2026-11-27) and SC-002's 'runs no coverage'.

decisions.summary: make lane's status (lane crate log.rs repairs_open) lists a superseded repair as open; not fixed here, filed as T65 to land before T23
decisions.why: A status line that names a repair no command offers is a wrong answer (a defect), but it is in the lane crate T15/T18 own, filed with a landing order before T23, not carried past the feature; nothing the GM asked for is narrowed by fixing it in its own task.

decisions.summary: Pins counted one a batch and keyed by (feature, task); a bundle's change pins each of its tasks; a change no hand-in names pins nothing; ejections with why red, inferred or unplaced count.
decisions.why: How the plan's D6 tripwire identifies a task's repeat ejection; it changes nothing the GM asked for. The request's red path (eject the failing change, land the rest, return it as a repair entry) is kept, and a task is still returned as a repair, now through the arbiter's ruling.

decisions.summary: The held change's own eject line (no repair, the trigger it waits on) is the hold; the batch's stop line lists it as held, so other changes read waiting and land in the next batch.
decisions.why: Data-model mechanics. Per the end-to-end test, an innocent hand-in lands while a held change waits, so the hold does not block the rest of the batch. That is the request's 'the rest of the batch lands'.

decisions.summary: The ruling is read from the clone's specs/<spec>/arbiter.jsonl, where make arbiter-ruled writes it, not from the lane's tree, which is reset to origin/main each batch.
decisions.why: Says where an existing record is read from. No scope change.

decisions.summary: The runner stops at the trip, and its next start (make lane-start or a hand-in's own start) files the ruling's repair.
decisions.why: Takes the plan's 'the lane stops' literally. A hand-in's own start restarts the runner, so other work is not held waiting on the coordinator, and the coordinator gets one owed line, which is FR-005's wake 'otherwise only for US5's cases'.

decisions.summary: A third pin asks the arbiter under its own trigger lane-<task>-<n>; a bundle's tasks are joined in the subject.
decisions.why: Needed because arbiter-ask refuses a trigger that has already been ruled. A naming choice with no change to what is asked.

decisions.summary: The ruling's eject line carries of_batch, not batch, so the three readers do not read a closed batch as reopened.
decisions.why: Internal field naming, recorded in data-model.md. No scope effect.

decisions.summary: An ask the arbiter refuses still stops the batch and holds the change, and the owed line names the make arbiter-ask command to run by hand. No retry.
decisions.why: The fallback still ends in one owed line naming the action, and no check or route is dropped (FR-008).

decisions.summary: The WHY text avoids the pool-route words that arbiter bundle --check-ask would refuse without a pool result.
decisions.why: A wording convention so that an existing check accepts the ask. No scope effect.

decisions.summary: Fixes a defect in the T15 tests: their stand-in Phase line had no newline, so a second red attempt's line was glued to the first. The new tests write it with its newline.
decisions.why: A known defect fixed on the way, as the fix-as-we-go rule asks. The old tests are unchanged.

decisions.summary: Detect a rebuilt binary by comparing device+inode of /proc/self/exe with the start path, and exec the path again, rather than stamping a binary id on each sample for readers to filter.
decisions.why: A design choice inside a defect fix (samples computed by code a landing replaced, 215 such samples observed 2026-11-27). It removes the stale-sample hole rather than filtering it, so it serves FR-010's like-window readings (T31) without narrowing anything the GM asked; the 'content id' it stands in for is T59's brief, not the GM's words.

decisions.summary: The re-run is an exec of the same process: pid and pid file kept, hours counted from --first so L7R_SAMPLE_MAX_H still bounds the whole run, and the re-run logged.
decisions.why: Keeps 451 T274's D3 (pid file names the sampler) and D13 (the hours bound a run) intact; no existing guarantee is relaxed.

decisions.summary: A missing path is no rebuild and an exec that returns (ETXTBSY etc.) is ignored: sample in the old code and retry at the next sample, with no log line per failed try.
decisions.why: A failure-handling choice that keeps sampling rather than stopping silently; the transient cases it names (cargo mid-write) clear by the next interval. Nothing the request or spec asks is left out; the no-log choice is a design call, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: The fix's claim is the BUILT binary at the sampler's path within one interval, not the source; scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh builds only at its next call after a landing.
decisions.why: An honest statement of the fix's reach, recorded in the module note and the audit. The source-to-build lag is the build script's existing behavior, outside T61's filed defect (the sampler running its start-time code for its whole hours) and not something the GM's request speaks to.

decisions.summary: After T59, before T31 (which reads the like window).
decisions.why: Sequencing so T31's FR-010 like window is not read from replaced code; serves the request.

decisions.summary: After landing, the clone's sampler is stopped and started once (pre-fix code cannot re-run itself), then a later landing must show 'runs its rebuilt binary' in sampler.log.
decisions.why: Operational step and a measured done-check; adds no scope.

decisions.summary: Counted as performance work under 451 FR-013 as a measurement tool.
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work that measures where the builders' time goes; the sampler measures the builders' memory, which bears on how many builders the pool runs. A scheduling classification, not a change to what is built; it narrows nothing the GM asked. Noted: FR-013's words are 'where the time goes', so the classification rests on the sampler serving builder throughput.

decisions.summary: Archive markers are judged apart from a section's words (words merged, the clone's tail of blank lines and markers kept), rather than archived sections looked up through a marker's range, plan-done.md and the archive's parts as the task line sketched.
decisions.why: A choice of mechanism serving the lane's purpose in the request (sketch item 1, FR-003, SC-001: a batch carried and pushed with no coordinator turn between). Neither request.md (the whole request) nor any requirement asks for a lookup, so departing from that sketch narrows nothing asked; measured on the T71 case, the lookup would leave the very stop red, so the chosen rule reaches the goal the lookup could not.

decisions.summary: The clone's markers win; a builder's own change to a marker is dropped for the clone's.
decisions.why: Merge mechanics. Only a landing writes the markers (FR-044's archive step), on the clone's side, so the clone's copy is the authoritative one; no check is dropped (FR-008) and nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Markers standing among a section's words stop where the builder's words are taken.
decisions.why: A stop for a merge no rule can decide (which of the builder's lines a marker follows). The block's dated census (an awk scan of every specs/*/plan.md, 2026-11-28) finds that shape only in 374's plan, which no carry touches, so no lane batch reaches it and no defect is left; a case that did arise would be the rare judgment case the request's sketch (item 3) and FR-005/US5 route to a wake, and FR-008 keeps every check.

decisions.summary: A section the clone archived and the builder changed still stops, and one the builder left alone is dropped, both as before; a section the builder removed now hands the clone's markers in it to the text before it.
decisions.why: The two arms kept as before are the existing section rule (451 T300, T419), each stop kept; a builder editing a finished, archived section is a real conflict and a judgment case, as the request provides. Handing a removed section's markers on is new and keeps the landing's archive record (FR-044's generated line) without dropping anything.

decisions.summary: a pure halve.rs answers the next set; run_batch keeps one loop over carry/land/push; an unplaced first red writes its attribute line (how none) and starts the halving; ejection code moved to runner/run/eject.rs because run.rs reached 1,001 lines
decisions.why: structure only; the behavior is D6 step 2's 'None' case followed by step 3's halving, which is FR-004's 'else bisect' and the GM's 'it bisects and ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands'.

decisions.summary: the first half is the first len/2 of a set
decisions.why: D6's table read literally ([A B C] runs [A] then [B]); a bisection's split point is not something the request or spec fixes.

decisions.summary: a second half whose first half ran green inside a red parent is red without a run; one whose first half ran red is untested and runs
decisions.why: D6's table literally (n=4 bad B: B ejected after [A] green with no run of its own); the inference is sound because the parent's red ran on the same main the green half landed on.

decisions.summary: untested sets standing together at the front run as one set
decisions.why: D6 step 2's 'the rest runs again'; it is what keeps US4's ceil(log2 n)+1 bound, held by the pure test over every single bad change of n=1 to 8.

decisions.summary: an inferred single is ejected only once everything else has landed or been ejected; two inferred singles are each ejected inferred, in hand-in order, at the end
decisions.why: D6 step 3's 'the one left'; with two bad changes each single's inference rests on its own red parent whose green sibling landed, so each is pinned by its own run and no innocent change is ejected. FR-004 ejects the failing change(s); nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: a one-change batch red the record cannot place is ejected red with no further run
decisions.why: its first run was its own one-change run; data-model's pin rule; bisection of one has nothing left to split.

decisions.summary: the halving runs over every change that ran, not over D6 step 2's several candidates only; the candidate narrowing is filed as T78, to land before T27
decisions.why: It narrows how far US4/FR-004's 'first by the gate's own report' (as D6 quotes it) is used when a red unit names several changes. Ground: applying D6 step 2 literally now would run a candidate beside riders, a run D6 step 4's pin rule does not cover (it is no one-change run), so the tripwire's pins - what keeps repeated reds on the same work from escaping the lane - would be undefined; literal application would defeat that rule's purpose. Against the request's purpose nothing is lost: the halving over every change still ejects only the bad change and lands the rest, within US4's bound for the batch's n (the pure test over every single bad change of n=1 to 8), so no wrong outcome is left. The block states T78 carries the narrowing and lands before T27; neither is in the bundle, so that ordering is the block's statement, not verified here.

decisions.summary: a first-pass row naming several changes is unplaced and halved over every change that ran; T15 Decision 6's single unplaced entry over the named changes is retired; the narrowing to the named changes joins T78
decisions.why: The same departure as Decision 6 and legitimate on the same ground (the candidate path needs a rider pin rule D6 step 4 lacks). Retiring the whole-group entry moves toward the request: a named change refused wherever it runs is ejected red after its own one-change run and the innocent ones land, as the pinned test shows.

decisions.summary: a first-pass row naming one change of the batch is placed: that change is ejected red
decisions.why: D6 step 2's one-candidate path, literally.

decisions.summary: a first-pass row naming no change of the batch (a hold, a lock, an owed round of no task of it) stops the runner with the batch open, nothing ejected, resumed by the next lane-start once the hold clears - rather than D6 step 2's 'None: the halving runs over the batch'
decisions.why: A real except-when against D6 step 2's None case, ruled on the block's stated reason (the T15 ruling it cites is not in the bundle). Purpose-level: such a refusal is no change's red, every half meets the same refusal, so halving would eject every change of the batch one by one - the opposite of 'ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands'. Applying the rule literally would defeat the request's purpose. It also cannot be routed around: FR-008 keeps the same checks, so while the hold stands no set can land by any route. Nothing is dropped: the batch stays open and resumes when the hold clears, and nothing pushes ungated.

decisions.summary: LANE_RETRY (0) is handed into the halving; tested at 0 and 1
decisions.why: D6 step 5's GUESS knob, unchanged in value.

decisions.summary: a halving green set whose push fails runs again once; a second failure is the batch's integrate entry over that set (T19), and changes not yet run stay waiting for the next batch
decisions.why: the existing push-failure path (T19) applied inside the halving; the unrun changes are neither ejected nor dropped, they land with the next batch; nothing pushes ungated (FR-008).

decisions.summary: a runner killed mid-halving resumes what is left as one attempt and the halving starts again from that red
decisions.why: crash recovery; every change still either lands gated or is ejected by the same rules, so FR-004 and FR-008 hold.

decisions.summary: no attribute line inside a halving: each set's run line names its red units, the halving's ejections are their own repair entries
decisions.why: log shape only; data-model's attribute row is the first red's.

decisions.summary: A measurement writes its plan section and has it reviewed (make decide, plan review) before it hands in; the hand-in asks the section of a measurement as it does of a fix (section_of returns Owed, not Later), the record still asked beside it.
decisions.why: Item 2 of the sketch the GM called very sensible: builders submit only once their change is ready to land, and refusals are fixed by the builder that has the context. FR-002: the hand-in runs the landing's cheap first pass. The landing already refuses a measurement's stub section, so asking it at hand-in is that pass, moved to the builder with the context. It adds an ask and drops none (FR-008), so it narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Rejected alternative: the tick taking the measurement record in place of a section.
decisions.why: Rejecting it keeps the plan gate's and the Approach block's asks on every task. Taking it would have waived a check every other task owes, against FR-008. Choosing not to waive a check is not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Section::Later, set by nothing once D1 lands, is removed and the doc comments in refusal.rs, tick.rs and land/cheap.rs are restated.
decisions.why: Dead code removed as a consequence of D1. No behavior changes beyond D1's.

decisions.summary: The builder brief's measurement STOP POINT and HAND IN lines, and builder-brief.md's THE FOUR KINDS and hand-in paragraphs, tell a measurement to write and have reviewed its section before handing in, within the 2,000-character cap, pinned by the block test.
decisions.why: This is the instruction side of D1, so that the builder with the context answers the ask (US2). The test only fails when the requested behavior's text is missing or over its cap, which makes it enforcement, not scope.

decisions.summary: Pin the gate-write guard over two trees: the clone and the lane's sibling worktree (git worktree add --detach) with a fake gate copying run_gate's argv and cwd; let through a commit, an Edit and a make task-add in the clone, hold the same aimed into the lane's tree; unit test plus section 5 of the hooks suite.
decisions.why: This is the fixture D10 names word for word (a commit, an Edit and a make task-add in the clone let through, the same aimed into the lane tree held), and it serves FR-001 (the guard holds only writes to the tree being gated).

decisions.summary: Add task-add to MAKE_WRITE in gate_write_hooks.rs, held only where the walk places it in a gated tree; measured red-first: a task-add aimed into the lane's tree was let through and writes tasks.md/plan.md, which the tree check refuses (exit 1).
decisions.why: D10's fixture requires a task-add aimed into the lane tree to be held, and the measurement shows it was not: fixing it carries out FR-001 and D10 rather than adding scope. It does not reach past them: in the clone and wherever no gate runs it still passes (451 T79), so the spec's 'holds only' bound is kept.

decisions.summary: Other make targets that write a tracked file (task-withdraw, queue-add, gm-reviewed) are still let through when aimed into a gated tree; not fixed in T27; filed as T80, which lands before T29, each target's writes to be measured against the tree check first (make append is let through on purpose, 405 T41).
decisions.why: This is ordering inside the feature, and nothing the spec asks for is dropped: T80 is filed in 461 and lands before the next phase task. That these targets void a gate is only inferred from reading MAKE_WRITE, not measured, and make append shows a target that writes specs/ is not automatically a defect. Measuring first is the project's rule, so the deferral does not leave a known defect behind.

decisions.summary: After T26; lands with T75 in one hand-in; green = unit test, suite and make builder-checks; red = recorded and set down, an impossibility claim goes through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Sequencing and exit criteria only. They settle nothing the request or the spec leaves open in a way that narrows it.

decisions.summary: A carry-conflict repair entry is kind integrate, why conflict, units the conflicting files, pinning nothing; a labeled departure from D7's paragraph (kind fix).
decisions.why: The GM asked that the ejected task return to the queue as a repair entry, and that conflicts be fixed by a builder, not the coordinator. The entry's kind is an internal label the request does not set. D7's table names the carry conflict as a repair entry for a fresh builder without fixing its kind, and gives the analogous push failure kind integrate. The departure is from plan text, not from the request or the spec, and it is labeled. The interim cost, that the queue offers integrate entries as hand-briefed until T95, is a briefing step, not integration work in the coordinator's context. It is disclosed, filed as T95 and ordered before T29.

decisions.summary: The tree is put back by cherry-pick --abort and then a hard reset to the HEAD read before the carry, before any line is written.
decisions.why: A mechanism choice that serves FR-003 and the request's 'the rest of the batch lands': the next change's carry needs a clean tree. It drops nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The set's carry line keeps code 0, and its conflict field lists every ejected change's files.
decisions.why: Log encoding. A non-zero code keeps meaning a stop with the batch open. This is bookkeeping inside the spec's design, with data-model.md amended to match.

decisions.summary: A carry that fails with no unmerged path ejects its change (why carry). Only the lane's own tree's stops still stop the runner with the batch open and nothing ejected: exit -1, and the carry's refusal of unfinished work in the lane's tree (CARRY_REFUSED).
decisions.why: The request reads 'ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands'. Round 2 now ejects every carry failure that is evidence on the one named change: a commit not located, a pick that refused to start, a continue that failed, an end not verified. That answers round 1's 4b objection. Only two cases are kept as stops, and each was judged on its own. (a) Exit -1, where make could not start or was killed: no change is named, so there is no failing change to eject. Ejecting would remove an innocent change on no evidence, which defeats the rule's purpose of landing the innocent rest. (b) CARRY_REFUSED: the carry refuses unfinished work in the lane's own tree before it touches the change, so every change of the batch would be refused alike. Ejecting would empty the batch of innocent changes and would refuse their repairs too. In both, the rule 'eject the failing change' cannot be applied because no change failed. This is the same reading as T15's Decision 6 ruling (a stop only where no change is named), which was reached on that task's own plan-review rounds. The stop also does not persist past the cause: a non-zero carry code lets T55's start-time reset clean the tree on the next start.

decisions.summary: The carry's output is kept as attempts/<batch>-carry-<sha10>.log, which is the entry's attempt. A resume that conflicts on the same change overwrites it.
decisions.why: This gives the fresh builder the conflict output, which is what D7 says the repair carries. The overwrite rule is about gate attempts (D6 step 1) and does not reach a carry log. A re-carry of the same sha in the same batch can only follow a kill between the entry and its eject line, and it gives the same carry's output.

decisions.summary: A conflict with an earlier change of the same batch ejects the later change, and the earlier one lands. The owed line says 'stopped in conflict'.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 'ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands' applied directly: the change whose carry fails is ejected and the rest go on. Nothing is excepted.

decisions.summary: One owed line for each conflict entry, with the batch's end line after it.
decisions.why: T15 Decision 10's rule. FR-005 allows a wake outside a landed batch for US5's cases, and D7's table lists a carry conflict as one of them.

decisions.summary: A conflict inside a halving's set ends the halving. The survivors land or go red as a plain attempt (a red unplaced starts a fresh halving), and the rest of the batch runs as one.
decisions.why: The request's bisect, eject and land-the-rest all still happen: a red among the survivors starts a fresh halving, and the failing change is still ejected while the rest lands. US4's bound, which SC-003 cites, is stated for one bad change. A conflict ejection during a halving is a second faulty change that the bound does not describe. The extra runs are a cost, not a fidelity finding, and the decision drops nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: T81 builds the record and its one reader; no handout path rewired (T82), replay is T83; next/offer/idle/repairs::first unchanged here
decisions.why: A split of FR-011's work across tasks, each named; nothing of US6 is dropped, only sequenced.

decisions.summary: dev/builder-policy.txt committed as class perf, class bugfix, no feature line; any all/floor set by the GM's word; class perf listed before class bugfix
decisions.why: The GM asked to be ABLE to indicate such priorities ('I probably want to be able to indicate priorities like'); he set no feature's form, so a default with none is his words, and SC-007's 461-all policy is a replay fixture, not a committed line. Perf before bugfix is a tie-break inside one GM priority that he did not set; both still outrank everything else, and the order is the record's to change.

decisions.summary: make task-add BUGFIX=1 prefixes [bugfix]; bugfix read among the tags after the id as PERF_TAG reads [perf]
decisions.why: FR-011 names the tag and the filing flag; the split fix (Found and left) is a defect fixed in the step that found it.

decisions.summary: Rank order: class, then form (floor-unmet, all, share, floor-met), then caller's feature, then key name, then within-feature order
decisions.why: Classes first is the GM's 'priority over everything else regardless of what feature'; forms next carry his first two examples; prefer and name order are the rules FR-011 folds in, ranked below what the GM set.

decisions.summary: A floor not yet met ranks above all; a met floor ranks below share (takes only uncontended trees)
decisions.why: Where an all feature and an unmet floor stand at once, 'gets all builders it needs, other things get only what is left over' and 'always gets 1 builder' cannot both be honored literally - physically impossible, not merely awkward. 'Always' is the GM's own universal, and the narrowing of all is confined to the one tree the floor names; once met, the floor feature 'only fills the available builders if there is no contention', as he wrote. It only arises if the GM writes both lines.

decisions.summary: The classes outrank every form, an unmet floor included
decisions.why: The GM's words verbatim: 'priority over everything else regardless of what feature they are attached to'.

decisions.summary: A line with no note= is refused; a malformed record ranks as the default and names every bad line
decisions.why: Enforces FR-011's 'one record the GM's words set'; the record's parse test re-runs on its edit (Cargo reads), so a malformed record does not land, and the fallback never invents an order nobody wrote.

decisions.summary: No class line keeps the default perf-then-bugfix; class none alone ranks no class
decisions.why: Holds the standing performance-first rule (451 FR-013) and the 2026-11-28 classes against a record that only adds a feature line; class none is a GM-set change to the record, which FR-011 makes the only route.

decisions.summary: LANE_REPAIR_FIRST not read; a repair ranks by its own task's class and feature, first within its feature
decisions.why: FR-011's words for dropping repairs-first and ranking by class and feature below the classes; the order between a feature's repair and its own queue lines is not set by the GM or the spec, and first-within never crosses a class or a feature.

decisions.summary: #! order=queue not read: T549's commit was ejected and is not in this tree; a queue's order is step 5, below the classes
decisions.why: FR-011 puts a queue's own order below the classes in its own feature; the ejected rule is filed as T91 to land before T82. Its premise (1136054db4 absent from this tree, the header parsing as a comment) is taken as the plan states it; the bundle allows no repository read to measure it.

decisions.summary: Unlisted open boxes of all and floor-unmet features named with their make queue-add; unlisted perf and bugfix tasks of any active feature named in their class
decisions.why: Serves 'gets all builders it needs' and 'always gets 1 builder' - the motivating case's pick had no queue line - and the classes 'regardless of what feature'; share and met-floor features keep today's offer of their queue lines, which takes nothing the GM asked for away. The unlisted walk's missing wait-skip is a known defect filed as T94, landing before T82, the first task through which any path reads ranked. A queue that cannot be parsed hiding its feature's tasks, class tasks included, is the existing listed_in behavior carried over, not a new outcome.

decisions.summary: Within the performance class, a listed perf entry ranks before an unlisted perf task of the same feature
decisions.why: An order inside one class and one feature, which no GM word or requirement sets; no pick crosses a class or a feature.

decisions.summary: unlisted_of skips no waiting, after-open, lands-before or GM-held task; filed as T94, lands before T82
decisions.why: No caller can get a wrong pick from it before T94 lands: no handout path reads ranked until T82, and T94 is ordered before T82. The defect is fixed before the step where it would produce a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: Repair the carried T76/T26 open-batch test in rust/gate/crates/lane/src/batch/tests.rs by adding the `all: &all` field T63 made required on l7r_shared::lane_log::World (one inserted line, 33dde3d59d), leaving the test otherwise unchanged.
decisions.why: A carried done commit that no longer compiles against HEAD is a defect (a wrong outcome: the batch gate red on a compile failure). Joining the test to the current struct keeps the test and its checks (FR-008: nothing of the existing checks is dropped) and serves the lane's landing of carried hand-ins (FR-003). It neither weakens the test nor changes World; no request clause is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Done is `make builder-checks CRATE=rust/gate/crates/lane` green at a HEAD holding 33dde3d59d; red exit is recorded and set down, an impossibility claim going through `make arbiter-ask`.
decisions.why: Measures exactly the outcome the fix is for (the crate's tests compile and pass); adds no new verification scope and drops none.

decisions.summary: attribute.rs's reds reads each cover-step line '<path> - lines no test reaches: <lines>' from the attempt's output as one unit per file ('<file> cover-run'), and touches maps it to every change whose delta holds that exact path
decisions.why: FR-004 and the sketch's item 1 ask that a red batch be attributed first by the gate's own report and bisected only where that names none. A coverage gap is reported in the gate's output, not as a red Phase line (measured 2026-11-28: both cover-run Phase lines are code 0), so before this the record placed nothing and five innocent changes were ejected. Reading the file named in that output is attribution from the gate's own report, the same way D6 step 2 places a first-pass row by its file. It widens what can be placed and so ejects fewer innocent changes. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: the path is taken relative to the lane tree's root, raw or canonical; a path outside the tree is kept whole and names only a change touching that whole path
decisions.why: Mechanics of matching a printed path against a delta. A path that matches nothing stays unplaced and goes to the halving, so nothing is lost.

decisions.summary: attribute's verdict is unchanged (one change per unit places it; a file two changes touch, or none, stays unplaced for T24's halving); a file unit beside a red lint unit places each on its own change
decisions.why: Keeps D6 step 2 and step 3 as T24 built them. A unit this block cannot place goes to the bisection, as FR-004 requires. No behavior beyond the new unit kind changes.

decisions.summary: the red-first test is built from batch 462-3's own log lines and changes; the unit form is written into the module doc, data-model.md's units paragraph and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md's lane row
decisions.why: The test only fails when the requested attribution is absent: it read 0 units of 4 on the old code and 4 placed on the new (measured 2026-11-28, make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/lane ONLY=attribute::tests). That is enforcement of FR-004, and the doc updates record its form.

decisions.summary: LANE_WAIT_MAX is not priced: 32 waits all completed on a lane line, the longest 27.4 min, so no platform limit was found.
decisions.why: D9 prices a ceiling only if the platform ends the background command at a time limit, as a wake FR-005 does not list; with no limit found, adding none keeps FR-005's 'otherwise only for US5's cases' intact.

decisions.summary: The lane's 'landed' line reports minutes since the last resume, so FR-005's status line under-reports a resumed batch's time; left unfixed in T23 and filed as T99, landing before T31.
decisions.why: This is a defect (a status line answering wrongly), so leaving it needs a ruling. It is legitimate: T23 is a measurement and by its approach changes no source, so the fix cannot be done in this task without turning a read into a code change. And leaving it in this task does not defeat what the request asks: the status line still wakes the coordinator once a batch (FR-005's actual requirement, and the GM's token-cost purpose), T23's own figures come from lane.jsonl rather than from that line, and the fix is scheduled before T31, the like-window measurement whose figures would rely on it. The defect is filed with an order, not carried silently.

decisions.summary: make task-time books none of a lane batch's gate (461-3's 28.5-min run reads as 20.9 working minutes), so T23's task-line verify fails; the task closes on its own re-derivation check (step 9) and the fix is filed as T100, landing before T31.
decisions.why: A tool that answers short is a defect, and the task's verify line is not met, so this needs a ruling. The verify is the plan's, not the GM's or the spec's. What it stands for, landing time being measured correctly for FR-006/FR-010/SC-005's before-and-after comparison, is needed at T31's like window, and T100 is ordered before T31. T23's own figures (batches, gate minutes, waits, coordinator calls) come from lane.jsonl, the Phase lines and the transcript through its own scripts, not from task-time, so none of the figures it records is corrupted by the defect. The fix is a source change that this read-only task cannot make. The purpose survives.

decisions.summary: D5's one-feature-a-batch rule splits an interleaved queue into batches of one (462-5); recorded as a throughput lever to price as T101, not changed; LANE_MAX unmoved.
decisions.why: Not a defect: no wrong outcome, D5's accepted rule working as written. Leaving the accepted decision as it is narrows nothing, and pricing it later is the spec's own GUESS-knob route.
